proposals.title: Observation-only round 3: dominant GetUserTweets probe is a fully-cached fixed-shape index access with no query_execution lever

anomaly.unit: fraction of the 960s terminal budget (8 terminals x 120s)

proposals.configuration_cause: The dominant transaction GetUserTweets is a read-only shared-buffer index access: buffer_hit_ratio 0.99992, seq_scan 0/s, idx_scan ~22.9k/s, blks_read 0.000743/txn, temp_bytes 0, and the observed plan is a single Index Scan (est_rows 1.0, est_cost 8.45). None of the allowed planner/statistics/executor knobs (default_statistics_target, from_collapse_limit, join_collapse_limit, random_page_cost, seq_page_cost, effective_cache_size, jit, work_mem, temp_buffers) can change the executor path or per-row cost of a fully-cached fixed-shape index probe, so the incumbent already sits at the query_execution optimum for this transaction class.
proposals.mechanism: Closed-loop identity TPS = terminals / weighted-mean client latency. GetUserTweets issues 3,186,707 of ~3,630,272 transactions (88%) and owns 0.8813 of the 960s terminal budget (846.1s). It is read-only and never enqueues on the WAL/commit path, so the flagged wal_wait cannot explain the read tail: write_average_ms is 0.138, wal_write_time is 30.45ms/s (~1.0us per client transaction), wal_sync is 0/s, host_io some/full stall fractions are 0.0, and wal_waiting_backends is median 0 / p95 0 / max 1 of ~9 backends. The dominant term is therefore governed by count and cached-probe latency, neither of which any allowed query_execution knob moves.
proposals.query_effect: GetUserTweets read path: ~7.23 rows fetched per transaction from shared buffers (9.62 blks_hit/txn, 7.43e-4 blks_read/txn, 7.18e-6 ms blk_read_time/txn, 0 temp bytes); p50 166us, mean 265.5us, p99 2626us, max 31294us. The tail is the executor/OS micro-stall on a hot cached page, not a data-access cost any planner knob can lower.
proposals.expected_tps_effect: unchanged: with knob_changes=[] the configuration is bit-identical to the incumbent, so goodput_rps stays inside the observed 28,257.5-31,906.7 rps band (verified median 30,213.6).
proposals.expected_latency_effect: unchanged: GetUserTweets p50 ~166us and p99 ~2626us are within the incumbent replicate spread (p50 165/169/157us; p99 2451/2486/2280/2626us).

predictions.rationale: Closed-loop identity 8 terminals / 270us weighted mean = 29.6k rps reproduces the measured 29,589 rps. With knob_changes=[] no query_execution lever is applied, so throughput must remain within +/-5% of the 29,762.6-31,906.7 verified replicate band.

0.8813 = 846.1s of 960s at 3,186,707 transactions; incumbent replicates were 0.8798/0.8817/0.8787 (span 0.30pp). With identical config neither the call count nor the cached-probe mean (265.5us) can move, so the fraction stays within 3pp of 0.881.

p50 166us is a shared-memory index access (buffer_hit_ratio 0.99992, 9.62 blks_hit/txn, 7.43e-4 blks_read/txn, 0 temp bytes) at plan cost 8.45; no allowed statistics/planner/executor knob alters this executor path, so p50 stays within the +/-10% replicate tolerance (165/169/157us).

p99 2626us is executor/OS micro-stall on hot cached pages with zero lock waits (locks_waiting 0/0/0), zero conflicts and zero JIT activity (plan cost 8.45 << default jit_above_cost); no query_execution knob governs this path, so p99 stays within +/-10% of the 2280-2626us replicate span.

Mean WAL write is 0.138ms at 220 writes/s with host_io some/full stall fractions 0.0, wal_sync 0/s and checkpoint write/sync time 0; the WAL pipeline has no queue to relieve and this transaction class is read-only, so the mean should not move by 0.5ms.

The wal_wait alert rests on one instantaneous sample (median 0.0, p95 0.0, max 1 of ~9 backends over 149 samples) against 0.00745 WAL writes per client transaction; no query_execution reconfiguration targets a waiter at the noise floor, so the max should not rise by 1 or more backends.

alternatives.statement: The GetUserTweets p99 tail (2626us vs p50 166us) is per-query JIT compilation / executor startup overhead introduced by jit=on, and would collapse if jit were disabled.

The rare wall-clock maxima (InsertTweet max 37428us, GetUserTweets max 31294us) are genuine intermittent storage fsync stalls that the wal_wait alert is detecting, and a storage-side change would remove them.

cross_domain_requirements: memory_storage: confirm no storage-side queue by holding write_average_ms / host_io stall fractions under observation rather than changing WAL knobs
concurrency_maintenance: confirm the read tail is not buffer-pin/LWLock contention via per-class wait-event sampling on the exact GetUserTweets SQL
proposals.why_exceeds_incumbent: It does not claim to exceed the incumbent. This is an observation-only proposal (knob_changes=[]): the verified incumbent is healthy (0 failed, 0 timeouts) and the dominant term is a fully-cached, optimal-plan, read-only index probe whose cost is count-driven, so any query_execution perturbation would be unfounded and would only consume the measurement budget. The proposal sharpens the diagnosis by freezing falsifiable no-change predictions on the read path and the WAL path.

proposals.title: Hold memory/storage configuration (knob_changes=[]): WAL, checkpoint, bgwriter and host-I/O telemetry show no queued storage mechanism, the 'wal_wait' alert is a single-sample artifact, and the terminal-dominant transaction is read-only

anomaly.source: diagnostic_alerts[wal_wait] (severity high); pg_stat_activity gauge sampled 149 times over the round_002_observation run

proposals.configuration_cause: No configuration cause is supported for the flagged storage anomaly. The incumbent already carries a WAL/checkpoint/bgwriter posture consistent with a quiescent device: max_wal_size 3672 MB against min_wal_size 181 MB produced 0 forced checkpoints in 162.4 s (checkpoints_req 0/s, checkpoints_timed 0.0062/s), checkpoint_completion_target 0.83 spreads the one timed checkpoint (checkpoint_write_time = checkpoint_sync_time = 0), bgwriter_lru_maxpages 338 with bgwriter_delay 22 ms leaves buffers_clean at 0/s with only 6.45 backend-written buffers/s, shared_buffers 53504*8kB = 428 MB sustains a 0.99992 buffer hit ratio with 21.98 blks_read/s, and work_mem 15.4 MB / temp_buffers 10.1 MB produce 0 temp_bytes and 0 temp_files. wal_buffers 5.1 MB and wal_writer_delay 215 ms / wal_writer_flush_after 2.9 MB are irrelevant at 149.5 kB/s of WAL. The only storage-relevant settings that are non-default are inert at this concurrency: commit_delay 671 us with commit_siblings 12 cannot fire with at most 8 sibling terminals (numbackends max 9), and wal_sync_method open_datasync folds the flush into the measured 0.1382 ms write (hence sync_average_ms = null).
proposals.mechanism: The storage subsystem is demand-limited, not service-limited. WAL durability costs 220.29 writes/s * 0.13821 ms = 30.4 ms of device-synchronous write per second, i.e. 0.001029 ms per client transaction against a weighted client mean of 0.270 ms, and PFI/PSI host_io some/full stall fraction is 0.0 with blk_read_time 0.212 ms/s. Under wal_sync_method open_datasync every WAL write is an O_DSYNC device write, so sync_average_ms is necessarily null and the flush cost is already inside the 0.1382 ms write time - there is no hidden un-timed fsync queue, and no wait-event corroboration either (wal_waiting_backends median 0.0 / p95 0.0 / max 1 of ~9 backends; io_waiting_backends median 0.0 / p95 0.0 / max 1). No cache, spill, background-writer, WAL or checkpoint queue exists to relieve: temp_bytes 0, buffers_clean 0/s, checkpoint_write_time = checkpoint_sync_time = 0, buffer_hit_ratio 0.99992 with 21.98 blks_read/s. Throughput is therefore fixed by the closed-loop identity TPS = 8 terminals / 0.270 ms weighted mean = 29.6k rps, which reproduces the measured 29,589 rps, and the dominant term GetUserTweets (0.881 of the 960 s terminal budget, 3.19 M calls at 166 us median) is read-only and never enqueues on the commit path. The coarser overall p95 of 698 us is not masking a rare transaction that eats the terminal: the largest per-class tails are InsertTweet max 37,428 us and GetTweetsFromFollowing max 31,552 us within classes whose terminal_capacity_fraction is 0.022 and 0.039, so even those tails cannot be the throughput limiter.

intermediate_metrics.aggregation: mean per WAL write over 162.4 s

intermediate_metrics.source: BenchBase per-transaction latency accounting (count * mean_us / (8 terminals * 120 s))

proposals.query_effect: GetUserTweets is a pure shared-buffer index probe: 9.62 blks_hit and 7.23 tup_fetched per transaction, 7.2e-6 ms of blk_read_time per transaction, 0 temp bytes, on the same Index Scan (estimated_rows 1.0, estimated_cost 8.45) the round-1/round-2 evidence recorded. Its 166 us median and 2,626 us p99 are executor and 8-terminal queueing time, not storage service time; InsertTweet is the only class that touches WAL and it moves only 5.05 WAL bytes and 0.00745 WAL writes per client transaction.
proposals.expected_tps_effect: No change: 8 terminals / 0.270 ms weighted mean = 29.6k rps, matching the measured 29,589 rps inside the incumbent replicate band (29,762.6-31,906.7, median 30,213.6). There is no storage queue to remove.
proposals.expected_latency_effect: No change beyond replicate noise: GetUserTweets p50 157-169 us, GetUserTweets p99 2,280-2,813 us, InsertTweet p99 3,336-4,059 us. A storage knob would have to act on a subsystem whose per-transaction cost is ~1.03 us.

predictions.rationale: With knob_changes=[] the re-measurement is bit-identical to the incumbent, so the closed-loop identity TPS = 8 / weighted mean latency is untouched. The four observed runs of this exact config span 28,257.5-31,906.7 rps (12.9% max/min); a +-10% window brackets that spread. Storage demand is 30.4 ms of WAL write per second and 21.98 blks_read/s, far below any queueing threshold.

0.8813 = 846.1 s of 960 s terminal time at 3,186,707 calls; incumbent replicates were 0.8798 / 0.8817 / 0.8787 (span 0.30 pp). This read-only class never enqueues on the WAL/checkpoint/bgwriter paths and carries only 7.2e-6 ms of blk_read_time per transaction with 0 temp bytes, so no allowed memory/storage knob can move the fraction by 1 pp.

Measured 0.13821 ms mean per WAL write at 220.29 writes/s and 149.5 kB/s with host_io some/full stall fraction 0.0, blk_read_time 0.212 ms/s and checkpoint write/sync time 0. The WAL path has no backlog to drain, so the per-write mean should not move by 0.5 ms (3.6x the observed value).

The flagged wait is one instantaneous sample: median 0.0, p95 0.0, max 1 of ~9 backends over 149 samples, with io_waiting_backends and lock_waiting_backends also at max 1 and 0. A hold-the-incumbent re-measurement cannot remove a waiter that is already at the noise floor, so the max should not rise by 1 backend or more.

InsertTweet p99 is 4,059 us on 0.00745 WAL writes and 5.05 WAL bytes per client transaction, with the entire WAL write budget at 0.00103 ms per client transaction and no measurable sync component (sync_average_ms null because open_datasync folds the flush into the 0.1382 ms write). The commit durability path is not the tail driver, so its p99 stays within the +-20% span already observed across replicates (3,336-4,059 us).

alternatives.statement: The 'wal_wait' alert and the InsertTweet tail (p99 4,059 us, max 37,428 us) are genuine rare device-level flush stalls that the per-write mean of 0.1382 ms hides, because wal_sync_method=open_datasync issues one O_DSYNC device write per WAL write and gives PostgreSQL no group-commit batching and no timed sync measurement (sync_average_ms is null). Under this reading, switching wal_sync_method to fdatasync - so concurrent committers can piggyback on one device flush and the sync path becomes timed - would cut the commit-path tail.

The anomaly is host-level dirty-page writeback pressure rather than a WAL queue: dirty_bytes reached p95 1.12 GB and max 1.24 GB while writeback_bytes peaked at only 7.5 MB and buffers_clean stayed at 0/s, so backends evict dirty buffers inline (buffers_backend 6.45/s). Under this reading, absorbing eviction work in the background writer (bgwriter knobs) rather than in backends would lower the per-transaction backend-write rate that is throttling the tail.

cross_domain_requirements: query_execution: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, TIMING) for the exact GetUserTweets SQL, to attribute the 2,626 us p99 to executor time versus any storage wait, since the supplied plan evidence is EXPLAIN without ANALYZE.

concurrency_maintenance: per-class wait_event sampling (LWLock:BufferContent, WALWrite, IO, ClientRead) at 8 terminals, because the wal_wait alert rests on one pg_stat_activity sample and the wait gauges cannot separate closed-loop client idle from a real WAL write wait.
proposals.why_exceeds_incumbent: It does not claim to exceed the incumbent and deliberately does not perturb it: every storage-relevant signal sits at the noise floor (30.4 ms of WAL device-write per second, 0.0 host_io stall, 0 checkpoint write/sync time, 0 buffers_clean/s, 0 temp bytes, 0.99992 buffer hit ratio) and the single wal_wait sample is uncorroborated by wal_timing, wait events and host_io read together. Spending a measurement on an unsupported storage knob would move nothing and would risk a real regression, for example lowering commit_siblings below the observed sibling count would activate the incumbent's 671 us commit_delay on every commit. The value delivered is refuting the high-severity wal_wait alert with three independent signals and redirecting the next measurement to the only lever that matters, the read-only GetUserTweets executor path already holding 0.881 of terminal capacity.

proposals.title: No concurrency/maintenance lever exists on the verified incumbent: lock, connection, deadlock, conflict and autovacuum pressure are all measured at zero; the terminal budget is owned by a read-only class (observation-only)
proposals.configuration_cause: No configuration cause is supported inside the concurrency_maintenance domain. The incumbent's concurrency and maintenance knobs (max_connections=137 vs observed numbackends max 9; max_locks_per_transaction=256 and max_pred_locks_per_transaction=4096 with locks_waiting 0/0/0 and lock_waiting_backends max 0; deadlocks 0/s and conflicts 0/s; autovacuum_max_workers=5, autovacuum_naptime=21s, autovacuum_vacuum_cost_delay=7.57ms, autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit=1064 against n_dead_tup 0/s and autovacuum_count 0.031/s) govern pressure that is measured absent. The 0.881 terminal share is a property of GetUserTweets call frequency (~3.19M of ~3.6M transactions) on a cache-resident index probe, not of any lock, connection, commit-queue or maintenance setting.
proposals.mechanism: Closed loop identity: TPS = 8 terminals / weighted-mean client latency. The waiting_backends gauge (median 2, p95 7, max 7) resolves almost entirely into client_waiting_backends (max 6) and idle_in_transaction (median 0, p95 3, max 4) on ~9 backends, i.e. BenchBase terminals waiting for their own next request, not backends queued on a server lock, WAL or buffer resource. lock_waiting_backends max is 0, locks_waiting is 0/0/0, deadlocks and conflicts are 0/s, and the only WAL wait sample (wal_waiting_backends max 1 of 9 over 149 samples, median 0, p95 0) coincides with write_average_ms 0.138 and host_io some/full stall fraction 0.0, so there is no queue anywhere in the concurrency or maintenance subsystem for a knob to drain. With no queue, every allowed autovacuum/connection/lock knob is inert on the dominant read-only path and can only add variance.
proposals.query_effect: GetUserTweets is a read-only cached index probe (p50 166us, p95 637us, p99 2626us; buffer_hit_ratio 0.99992; blk_read_per_txn 0.00074; temp_bytes_per_txn 0; plan = Index Scan, est_rows 1.0, est_cost 8.45). It holds no heavyweight lock beyond AccessShare, takes no XID, writes no WAL, and never enters the commit queue, so no concurrency or maintenance knob in the allowed set changes its per-call cost.
proposals.expected_tps_effect: Unchanged: the incumbent is re-measured bit-identically, so goodput stays inside its own replicate band (verified 29,762.6-31,906.7 rps, median 30,213.6; observation run 29,589.3 rps).
proposals.expected_latency_effect: Unchanged: GetUserTweets p50/p95/p99 and all per-class terminal shares stay within their observed replicate spread because no knob atom is altered.

predictions.rationale: knob_changes=[] leaves the configuration bit-identical, so the closed-loop identity TPS = 8 / weighted-mean latency is untouched; the four observed runs of this exact config span 28,257.5-31,906.7 rps (12.7% span), so an 8% tolerance is the tightest defensible no-op bound.

0.8813 = 846.1s of the 960s terminal budget; the three verified baselines gave 0.8798/0.8817/0.8787 (span 0.3pp). Neither the call count (~3.19M) nor the mean latency (265.5us) is moved by any allowed concurrency/maintenance knob, so the fraction stays within 3pp.

locks_waiting is 0/0/0, lock_waiting_backends max is 0 and GetUserTweets holds only AccessShare on a static snapshot; with no knob change there is no lock conflict to create or relieve, so the max must not rise by 1 backend.

The workload is insert-only on a restored snapshot: n_dead_tup is 0/s and autovacuum_count is 0.031/s against autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.128; holding the maintenance knobs leaves that background rate within 25% of 0.031/s over a 120s window.

The wal_wait alert rests on one instantaneous sample: median 0.0, p95 0.0, max 1 of ~9 backends across 149 samples, against wal_write 220/s and write_average_ms 0.138 with host_io some/full stall fraction 0.0. No commit/WAL/concurrency knob can remove a waiter already at the noise floor, so the max should not rise by 1 backend.

client_waiting_backends max 6 alongside idle_in_transaction max 4 and waiting_backends max 7 shows the wait gauge is BenchBase terminal idle, not a server resource wait; no concurrency/maintenance knob governs client think time, so the max stays within 1 backend of 6.

alternatives.statement: The GetUserTweets tail is caused by heavyweight row/relation lock waits on the writer path (InsertTweet) blocking the dominant read class, so a lock-sizing knob should relieve it.
A genuine WAL flush stall (the wal_wait alert) serializes the commit path and spills into the reader tail, so wal_writer/commit knobs should relieve it.
Autovacuum/autoanalyze on a growing heap contends for buffers and I/O with the read class, so aggressive autovacuum knobs should relieve it.

The read tail is lightweight-lock contention (buffer-mapping / ProcArray / snapshot LWLock) that heavyweight lock metrics cannot see, so it would require session/connection-level concurrency changes rather than loud lock waits.

cross_domain_requirements: Per-class wait_event_type/wait_event sampling for the GetUserTweets SQL (currently only aggregate waiting_backends is available, so LWLock attribution is not observable from the concurrency domain).
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) plus plan-level p99 for the exact GetUserTweets statement to separate execution cost from queueing.
proposals.why_exceeds_incumbent: It does not need to beat the incumbent's throughput; it must avoid a regression. Every allowed concurrency/maintenance change targets pressure measured at zero (0 lock waiters, 0 deadlocks, 0 conflicts, 9 of 137 connections, 0.031 autovacuum/s, 0/s dead tuples), so any such change can only inject variance into a workload whose constraint is the frequency of a read-only cached index probe. Holding the incumbent preserves the verified 29,762.6-31,906.7 rps band (median 30,213.6) and the 0.881 terminal share within its observed 0.3pp spread.

payload.title: Hold memory/storage configuration (knob_changes=[]): WAL, checkpoint, bgwriter and host-I/O telemetry show no queued storage mechanism, the 'wal_wait' alert is a single-sample artifact, and the terminal-dominant transaction is read-only

anomaly.source: diagnostic_alerts[wal_wait] (severity high); pg_stat_activity gauge sampled 149 times over the round_002_observation run

payload.mechanism: The storage subsystem is demand-limited, not service-limited. WAL durability costs 220.29 writes/s * 0.13821 ms = 30.4 ms of device-synchronous write per second, i.e. 0.001029 ms per client transaction against a weighted client mean of 0.270 ms, and PFI/PSI host_io some/full stall fraction is 0.0 with blk_read_time 0.212 ms/s. Under wal_sync_method open_datasync every WAL write is an O_DSYNC device write, so sync_average_ms is necessarily null and the flush cost is already inside the 0.1382 ms write time - there is no hidden un-timed fsync queue, and no wait-event corroboration either (wal_waiting_backends median 0.0 / p95 0.0 / max 1 of ~9 backends; io_waiting_backends median 0.0 / p95 0.0 / max 1). No cache, spill, background-writer, WAL or checkpoint queue exists to relieve: temp_bytes 0, buffers_clean 0/s, checkpoint_write_time = checkpoint_sync_time = 0, buffer_hit_ratio 0.99992 with 21.98 blks_read/s. Throughput is therefore fixed by the closed-loop identity TPS = 8 terminals / 0.270 ms weighted mean = 29.6k rps, which reproduces the measured 29,589 rps, and the dominant term GetUserTweets (0.881 of the 960 s terminal budget, 3.19 M calls at 166 us median) is read-only and never enqueues on the commit path. The coarser overall p95 of 698 us is not masking a rare transaction that eats the terminal: the largest per-class tails are InsertTweet max 37,428 us and GetTweetsFromFollowing max 31,552 us within classes whose terminal_capacity_fraction is 0.022 and 0.039, so even those tails cannot be the throughput limiter.

alternatives.statement: The 'wal_wait' alert and the InsertTweet tail (p99 4,059 us, max 37,428 us) are genuine rare device-level flush stalls that the per-write mean of 0.1382 ms hides, because wal_sync_method=open_datasync issues one O_DSYNC device write per WAL write and gives PostgreSQL no group-commit batching and no timed sync measurement (sync_average_ms is null). Under this reading, switching wal_sync_method to fdatasync - so concurrent committers can piggyback on one device flush and the sync path becomes timed - would cut the commit-path tail.

The anomaly is host-level dirty-page writeback pressure rather than a WAL queue: dirty_bytes reached p95 1.12 GB and max 1.24 GB while writeback_bytes peaked at only 7.5 MB and buffers_clean stayed at 0/s, so backends evict dirty buffers inline (buffers_backend 6.45/s). Under this reading, absorbing eviction work in the background writer (bgwriter knobs) rather than in backends would lower the per-transaction backend-write rate that is throttling the tail.

payload.title: No concurrency/maintenance lever exists on the verified incumbent: lock, connection, deadlock, conflict and autovacuum pressure are all measured at zero; the terminal budget is owned by a read-only class (observation-only)
payload.mechanism: Closed loop identity: TPS = 8 terminals / weighted-mean client latency. The waiting_backends gauge (median 2, p95 7, max 7) resolves almost entirely into client_waiting_backends (max 6) and idle_in_transaction (median 0, p95 3, max 4) on ~9 backends, i.e. BenchBase terminals waiting for their own next request, not backends queued on a server lock, WAL or buffer resource. lock_waiting_backends max is 0, locks_waiting is 0/0/0, deadlocks and conflicts are 0/s, and the only WAL wait sample (wal_waiting_backends max 1 of 9 over 149 samples, median 0, p95 0) coincides with write_average_ms 0.138 and host_io some/full stall fraction 0.0, so there is no queue anywhere in the concurrency or maintenance subsystem for a knob to drain. With no queue, every allowed autovacuum/connection/lock knob is inert on the dominant read-only path and can only add variance.

alternatives.statement: The GetUserTweets tail is caused by heavyweight row/relation lock waits on the writer path (InsertTweet) blocking the dominant read class, so a lock-sizing knob should relieve it.
A genuine WAL flush stall (the wal_wait alert) serializes the commit path and spills into the reader tail, so wal_writer/commit knobs should relieve it.
Autovacuum/autoanalyze on a growing heap contends for buffers and I/O with the read class, so aggressive autovacuum knobs should relieve it.

The read tail is lightweight-lock contention (buffer-mapping / ProcArray / snapshot LWLock) that heavyweight lock metrics cannot see, so it would require session/connection-level concurrency changes rather than loud lock waits.
